key_insight: Detonation-sprayed Fe-based amorphous coatings with more circular, well-spread droplets form denser microstructures that improve corrosion resistance and reduce wear, especially in humid environments.
engineering_relevance: Controlling spray parameters to minimize porosity is critical for producing durable protective coatings on carbon steel for corrosive and humidity-variable service conditions.
method: Detonation spray Fe-based amorphous coatings onto Q235 carbon steel under varied parameters
Compare droplet morphology, coating microstructure, porosity, corrosion behavior, and tribological performance
Test wear against Si3N4 balls across different humidity levels
evidence_signal: The abstract reports systematic corrosion and wear testing and links lower porosity with better long-term corrosion resistance, while higher humidity reduces friction coefficient and wear rate.
watch_item: Performance depends strongly on spray-induced defect levels, so process control is essential because higher porosity can quickly undermine long-term corrosion durability.
paper_title: Long-term corrosion behaviors and wear behavior of Fe-based amorphous coatings in different humidity environments
